tail:
Step 6 audit complete. All gates clean, `library/` untouched, no status flipped.

## What I audited

The 37 draft items, all published items they cite, and the six items already on the pair. I dispatched **six read-only proof-refuters** (no brief template existed, so I authored one) in clusters covering all 37 items with no gaps — on top of the two step-6a readers, who had found no fatal defect.

## Fatal defects — five, all confirmed from disk, all repaired

**Overstated Statements/titles (3):**
- **`ex-presentation-of-a-dihedral-group`** — the run's strongest finding. It defined `D_n` as "the symmetry group of a regular n-gon, of order 2n", asserted it is generated by ρ and σ, then proved only that the presentation matches `⟨{ρ,σ}⟩ ≤ Sym(ℤ/n)`. This library develops no plane isometries, so the named target wasn't an object it has — the same failure mode as D2. Repaired by making `D_n` stipulative, so order 2n is now *proved*, not assumed.
- **`thm-abelianisation-of-a-free-group-is-free-abelian`** — title said "**the** free abelian group" where only "**a**" is proved. Unlike free groups, this library has no uniqueness theorem for free abelian groups, so the definite article was unlicensed. Title corrected.
- **`ex-presentation-of-z-squared`** — Statement asserted ℤ² *is* "the free abelian group on two generators", a universal property no step proves. Reworded.

**Citation-licensing raised as fatal (2):** `ex-free-group-on-the-empty-set` and `ex-free-group-on-one-generator` quantified over all free groups but proved only the word model. I classified these nonfatal — the bridge is one citation of a theorem on the same page — but repaired them anyway, since step 6 permits polish and their sibling already did it correctly. Both Statements are now strictly stronger.

Plus seven fact-fidelity repairs where a displayed `[F#]`/`[L#]` omitted the exact clause its proof used.

## The D6 spine

The van der Waerden argument is **non-circular** — verified independently by me and both spine refuters: both composition orders are proved, and uniqueness comes from evaluating at the empty word, never from the normal form under proof. The published `def-free-group` is not reconvention'd anywhere.

## Two things needing you

1. **The staged amendment was incomplete.** It changed only the item lists, but the A-page summary was written for today's six items — applying the lists alone would publish a page failing the summary contract. I staged a replacement summary; the owner's publish action is now four steps, not three.
2. **Twice-touched: `ex-presentation-of-a-dihedral-group`** (repaired 2×) needs your personal audit. Both repairs were mine in one sitting and the second was a one-sentence cosmetic rephrase clearing a `prosecheck` warning my own first wording introduced — a bookkeeping artifact, not two refutations.

**Honest gap:** while iterating I ran `git checkout` on the batch proof-contracts file, discarding the readers' *uncommitted* step-6a edits to it. I recovered by regenerating all 29 entries' citations and derivations mechanically from current item text (strict passes at 0 errors, and this is more accurate than a hand-maintained map), but any boundary-record adjustments they made there are lost. Also flagged: `finite-smoke` registers zero executable checks, and contract boundary dispositions are weak records — details in §9 of `research/freegroups-1-alpha-report.md`.

**Step-7 rejudge set — 13 ids**, listed in §3 of the report:
`cor-every-finite-group-is-finitely-presented`, `def-free-abelian-group`, `def-word-quotient-model-of-the-free-group`, `ex-free-group-on-one-generator`, `ex-free-group-on-the-empty-set`, `ex-presentation-of-a-dihedral-group`, `ex-presentation-of-z-squared`, `thm-abelianisation-of-a-free-group-is-free-abelian`, `thm-conjugacy-of-cyclically-reduced-words`, `thm-finite-free-bases-have-the-same-cardinality`, `thm-free-groups-are-torsion-free`, `thm-normal-form-for-the-word-quotient-model`, `thm-word-quotient-model-is-free`.

I added no new item, so authored no new proof; changed no id, reading order, status, or page file.
